- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecast shows gradual upward trend, while true values often spike higher mid-period or show sharp drops later — model fails to capture volatility.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices (e.g., after 85+), forecasting continued rise instead of mean reversion.
- Model lags behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model tends to overestimate the “recovery” phase after sharp drops — overshoots by 1–3 points before correcting.
- True outcomes often show a “rebound” or “reset” after a low, while model continues upward trend.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or event-driven price corrections — e.g., after 80–82, true price often drops below 75, model doesn’t adjust.
- Model assumes linear progression, while true price exhibits non-linear, noisy behavior with clustering around 80–85 range.
- Model underestimates the impact of “low-activity” periods — e.g., when true price drops below 75, model doesn’t recognize it as a signal to adjust downward.
- Model overfits to recent high values, ignoring historical mean or long-term trend.
